data.long_meaning: An occasion when something is made clear or revealed. In Christian tradition, it refers to the revelation of God in the form of a child, Jesus Christ, to the Gentiles.
data.spiritual_meaning: A moment of profound understanding or illumination

in_hebrew.name: אפיפניה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אפיפניה נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'אפיפניה', שפירושה הופעה או התגלות. הוא מתייחס להתגלותו של אלוהים בבשר, במיוחד בהקשר של לידתו של ישוע המשיח. השם קשור לחג האפיפניה הנוצרי, המציין את ביקורם של החכמים ממזרח, הידועים גם כמלכים, בישוע התינוק.

in_greek.name: Επιφάνεια
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Επιφάνεια προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'επιφάνεια', που σημαίνει εμφάνιση ή αποκάλυψη. Αναφέρεται στην εμφάνιση του Θεού σε σάρκα, ιδιαίτερα στο πλαίσιο της γέννησης του Ιησού Χριστού. Το όνομα συνδέεται με τη χριστιανική εορτή της Επιφάνειας, που εορτάζει την επίσκεψη των Μάγων από την Ανατολή, γνωστών επίσης ως βασιλέων, στο βρέφος Ιησού.

in_latin.name: Epiphania
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Epiphania derivatum est ex voce Graeca 'ἐπιφάνεια', quae significat manifestatio seu revelatio. Refertur ad manifestationem Dei in carne, praesertim in contextu nativitatis Iesu Christi. Nomen coniungitur cum festivitate christiana Epiphaniae, quae visitationem Magorum ab Oriente, regum etiam dictorum, ad infantem Iesum celebrat.

in_english.name: Epiphany
in_english.meaning: A manifestation or revelation of God in the flesh
in_english.long_meaning: The name Epiphany originates from the Greek word 'ἐπιφάνεια' (epiphaneia), meaning manifestation or revelation. It refers to the manifestation of God in the flesh, particularly in the context of the birth of Jesus Christ. The name is associated with the Christian feast of Epiphany, which commemorates the visit of the Magi, also known as the Three Wise Men or Kings, to the infant Jesus. The term 'Epiphany' has been used in Christian tradition since the 4th century to signify the revelation of Jesus Christ to the world. The name symbolizes spiritual awakening, divine revelation, and the acknowledgment of Jesus as the Son of God.

historical_references.reference: The Magi, also known as the Three Wise Men, visited the baby Jesus in Bethlehem. This event is celebrated as the Epiphany in the Western Christian tradition.
historical_references.context: 1st century AD - This event is believed to have occurred forty days after Jesus' birth, according to the Gospel of Matthew.

historical_references.reference: The manifestation of Christ to the Gentiles through the Magi was a significant event in early Christianity, as it symbolized the universality of God's love. The Eastern Orthodox Church continues to commemorate this event on January 6.
historical_references.time_period: 1st century AD - This event is believed to have occurred around the same time as the Magi's visit.
historical_references.context: Another interpretation of the Epiphany is the revelation of Jesus as the son of God to the Gentiles. This occurred when the Magi, who were from the East, came to pay homage to Jesus.

It commemorates the visit of the Magi to the baby Jesus, symbolizing the revelation of Jesus as the Son of God to the Gentiles. Modern observations of Epiphany can be seen on various platforms. In religious contexts, there are services and celebrations in churches and communities around the world. Epiphany is also a time for gift-giving and feasting, with families and friends gathering to share meals and exchange presents. Lastly, there are various decorations and symbolic gifts associated with Epiphany, such as the Epiphany tree, the three Magi, and the star of Bethlehem.
